seed: THE CLAIM: a section of the right hand panel says at most one short line, and only when that line tells you something you cannot see. Pick three boxes and the panel used to print seven lines of small grey prose before you reached a control: three under Appearance repeating a count the Layers list already shows, two under Effects naming what the plus does, two under Arrange. This walk picks three boxes with nothing turned on, reads the panel's own section geometry back (dockSections, dockViewport, dockInView) and takes a real capture, so the room this buys is a number rather than an opinion. Before: 1044pt of sections in an 868pt viewport, Position & Size 856-1044, entirely below the fold.

steps.note: Three boxes picked, nothing switched on. The Layers section already says '3 layers selected'. Under the rule, Appearance says nothing (the count and the reach are on screen already), Effects says one short line because an empty section reads as broken, and Arrange says nothing because lining up with each other is what picking three things means. Read the section geometry back: what matters is how far down Arrange starts and how many sections fit the dock whole.

The one thing here you cannot work out by looking is what Arrange lines up AGAINST. Group two of them and step into the group: the reference becomes the group rather than the selection, and it is said BESIDE the Arrange heading, where it costs no line and is still there when the section is collapsed.
